_meta: #115 Built-in WordPress security tutorial. Each entry = one teaching step shown in the GUI tutorial flow.

steps.title: Why WordPress security is hard
steps.body: WordPress runs ~43% of the web. Its plugin ecosystem (~60k plugins) means most security issues today are in third-party plugins, not core. Plugin developers ship at very different quality levels — a popular plugin with 1M+ installs may still have a critical CVE every few months.

steps.title: The four risk tiers
steps.body: WPSecScan reports findings as critical / high / medium / low / info. Critical = remote code execution, auth bypass, or data dump. High = privilege escalation, broken access control. Medium = info disclosure, missing hardening. Low = minor leaks. Info = configuration notes.

steps.title: Why we score 0-100
steps.body: The risk score deducts points for findings with severity-tier caps so one runaway check can't dominate. 90+ = healthy, 70-89 = a few issues, 40-69 = priority fixes needed, <40 = significant exposure. The grade (A-F) is for non-technical stakeholders.

steps.title: Passive vs aggressive
steps.body: Passive checks (default) read responses but never send active payloads. Aggressive (`--aggressive`) sends SQLi / XSS / SSRF probes — these CAN trigger WAF blocks or rate limits. Only use aggressive on sites you own or have written permission to test.

steps.title: Threat intel sources
steps.body: WPSecScan integrates with CISA KEV (known-exploited CVEs), EPSS (exploitation probability), VirusTotal (URL reputation), Sucuri SiteCheck, and the Wordfence DB. The KEV badge on a finding means active in-the-wild exploitation.

steps.title: The exploit playbook
steps.body: Every finding has a copy-paste playbook showing curl / sqlmap / Metasploit / nuclei / wpscan / ffuf commands. WPSecScan never executes these — you copy them to your own terminal. Defensive use only.

steps.title: Custom checks
steps.body: Drop Python files in ~/.wpsecscan/plugins/ to add your own checks. Drop YAML files in ~/.wpsecscan/templates/ for nuclei-style templates. Drop JS in plugins/ (Node required) for scriptable rules. Drop signatures in ~/.wpsecscan/signatures/ for plugin-CVE patches.

steps.title: Reporting + integrations
steps.body: Outputs: HTML, JSON, CSV, MD, XLSX, SARIF, HAR, Burp scope, executive PDF, customer attestation. Ships an HTTP API server, daemon mode, audit-log shipping to Splunk/Datadog/Loki, Slack/Discord webhooks, GitHub Issues auto-create.
